Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 168: Just You Wait 'Til We Get Home Tonight

After waiting in line for a few minutes, it was soon Li Luo and Ying Chanxi's turn.

Zhao Rongjun came over to act as their guide, handing a blindfold over. "This pink one is for girls."

"Thank you." Ying Chanxi took the blindfold and put it on her head. Before covering her eyes, she carefully studied the positions of the three dragons on the blackboard ahead.

Zhao Rongjun also told Ying Chanxi in a timely manner, "Your team is drawing the eyes on the dragon on the left. Just walk straight."

"Are you ready?" asked Li Luo from behind her. "It's useless no matter how long you look. You'll still need me to direct you."

"Hmph." Provoked by him, Ying Chanxi immediately covered her eyes with the blindfold and then said, "Let's go. Don't you dare mislead me just to win."

"I'm not you," Li Luo chuckled. "Go straight. Zhao Rongjun, help her with the time."

"Oh." Zhao Rongjun glanced at the clock on the wall and noted the time Ying Chanxi started. "Timing has begun."

"Got it." Once Ying Chanxi put on the blindfold, her vision went completely dark. As she walked forward, she subconsciously raised both her arms.

Even though she knew perfectly well that there was nothing in front of her, she was still cautious and didn't dare to walk too fast.

"There's nothing in front of you. I'll remind you when you're almost at the platform steps," Li Luo said from behind.

"I know, I know. Don't rush me."

When a person is plunged into darkness and loses their sight, it's easy to fall into a state of subconscious anxiety.

She had thought it was a very simple game, but unable to see anything and relying solely on her teammate's directions, it proved to be a little harder than Ying Chanxi had imagined.

"The steps are right ahead," Li Luo reminded her. "About a meter from your right foot. Yes, you can kick forward a bit to see where the step is."

Following Li Luo's instructions, Ying Chanxi successfully found the step, got onto the platform, and groped her way to the blackboard, feeling for a piece of chalk in the chalk tray.

"Where's the dragon?" Ying Chanxi raised her arm and asked Li Luo.

"Take one step to the left."

"Like this?"

"More to the left."

"Is that it?"

"You overshot it. Take half a step to the right."

"How about now?"

"Okay, stay still," Li Luo said. "Raise your right hand, higher. Good, touch the blackboard. Right there."

"Draw a circle, then move half a palm's width to the left and draw another one."

"Alright, take off the blindfold."

Following Li Luo's directions, Ying Chanxi finished drawing, then took off her blindfold to take a look.

On the blackboard, two vaguely shaped things that could generously be called eyes had been drawn on the dragon's head.

And because Ying Chanxi's right hand had shifted slightly as she moved it, the eyes were a bit uneven, looking quite awkward.

But the requirements for Class Three's mini-game weren't high to begin with. As long as it was passable, it was fine.

So when Luo Jiajia came over to inspect, she still gave Ying Chanxi a stamp.

"Two minutes and thirty-seven seconds," Zhao Rongjun said to the two after looking at the clock.

"That's considered fast, right?" Ying Chanxi hummed smugly. "Just get ready to bark like a dog."

"What's your hurry?" Li Luo chuckled. "Are you planning on being mischievous later to slow me down?"

"Of-of course not…" Having her little scheme exposed, Ying Chanxi's gaze immediately flickered with guilt. "My directing will definitely be better than yours."

"Is that so? But I'd rather hear you bark like a dog." Li Luo smiled. Instead of rushing to put on the blindfold Zhao Rongjun handed him, he asked, "Can I do a trial run first?"

"Huh?" Zhao Rongjun was stunned for a moment. "I guess so, but there's a huge difference between walking with and without a blindfold. A trial run won't be much use."

"You don't seriously think one run-through will be enough, do you?" Ying Chanxi added from the side. "When I put on the blindfold just now, I could barely even walk."

"Don't be so hasty. Trying doesn't cost anything." Li Luo looked down at the classroom floor, found the starting position, and lined up the tips of his shoes with the seam between the floor tiles.

Then he strode forward, walked all the way up to the platform, picked up a piece of chalk, and raised his hand to draw eyes on the dragon's head, which had since been erased.

But it wasn't enough for him to just draw on one dragon. He moved to the side and drew eyes on the other two dragons as well.

Then he placed the chalk back where he had picked it up and returned to the starting point.

"Alright, let's do this," Li Luo said, picking up the blindfold.

Ying Chanxi looked at him suspiciously. "That's it? If you can remember all that, I'll not only bark like a dog, but I'll also oink like a pig."

This wasn't just about memorizing information. It was one thing for Li Luo to have a good memory, but now his physical senses would be affected by the blindfold.

Ying Chanxi really didn't believe he could remember all of that.

"You said it yourself." Li Luo just smiled, then said, "I've memorized it. Don't forget the dog barks and pig oinks later. You can't miss a single one."

"Hmph, if you can't do it, then you have to do both too."

"I never said that. You said it yourself." Li Luo chuckled, already putting on the blindfold.

"If you don't agree to oink like a pig, then I'm not directing you," Ying Chanxi said in a huff, pouting her lips.

"I never said I needed you to direct me, either." Li Luo lifted the blindfold to glance at his feet, realigning them with the tile seam before covering his eyes again.

Then, after a moment of silence, Li Luo strode forward.

He moved so quickly that one might have thought he wasn't wearing a blindfold at all.

"Hey!" Ying Chanxi exclaimed in surprise. Just as she was about to call out to him, she saw Li Luo nearing the platform steps and grew even more anxious. "Be careful! The steps are right ahead! Don't fall!"

As she shouted, Ying Chanxi couldn't help but run forward, afraid that Li Luo would fall.

But Li Luo, as if he truly had X-ray vision, walked straight up onto the platform without the slightest pause.

Even his posture and movements when picking up the chalk, if someone had been able to recall them, they would find they were almost identical to his trial run.

And so, very quickly.

All three dragons on the blackboard had a pair of eyes drawn on them by Li Luo.

There was not the slightest discrepancy.

"Done." Li Luo took off the blindfold, looked at the blackboard, and nodded in satisfaction. "This should be good enough, right?"

Ying Chanxi, who had followed Li Luo and was standing below the platform, stared at the blackboard with her mouth agape, speechless for a moment.

It wasn't until Li Luo had his booklet stamped and came to stand in front of her, waving a hand before her eyes, that she gradually came back to her senses.

"How did you do that?" Ying Chanxi looked at Li Luo with suspicion, even taking the blindfold off his forehead to inspect it, deeply suspecting that he and Zhao Rongjun had conspired to cheat.

But after looking for a long time, it was just an ordinary blindfold. There was no way for the wearer to see the ground clearly.

Even if one wore it a bit loosely and could vaguely see the path below through the gap at the bottom, it would be impossible to draw the eyes on the blackboard so precisely.

"I already told you," Li Luo said, returning the blindfold to Zhao Rongjun. "I have X-ray vision."

"I'd have to be a fool to believe you," Ying Chanxi said, rolling her eyes at him.

"So, about the barking?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow. "A bet's a bet. And the pig oinks, you said that yourself."

At Li Luo's reminder, Ying Chanxi's face flushed red. She leaned close to him and whispered, "Y-you, keep your voice down. Can I do it for you when we get home?"

"Oh? What happened to all that arrogance from before?" Li Luo teased. "Why are you whispering all of a sudden?"

"Stop it," Ying Chanxi pouted angrily. "Who knew you were such a freak, acting like you have X-ray vision with a blindfold on."

"I'll spare your life for now," Li Luo chuckled. "Just you wait 'til we get home tonight."

"Hmph, I know, I know." Ying Chanxi was a little indignant, but she was willing to honor the bet. "I'll do it at home. Let's forget about it at school."

"Well, there are still the events for Class Four and our Class Eight. Let's finish them quickly and go for the prize draw," Li Luo said, no longer teasing her. He smiled and walked out of the classroom.

Ying Chanxi quickly followed.

After the two of them cleared Class Four's mini-game, they soon returned to Class Eight's classroom.

"Quick, quick," Ying Chanxi said, pulling him into Class Eight's room. "After we finish this one, we can go to the prize draw."

"What's the hurry?" Li Luo walked into the classroom and saw Yan Zhusheng still sitting in her chair, fiddling with the instrument in her hands.

Right then, however, she was holding the guitar Li Luo had brought and playing a 15-second melody with Ren Zheng beside her.

Li Luo glanced at the other people in the classroom and quickly found Xu Guangtao, who was in charge of stamping. He walked over to his side and patted his shoulder, signaling for the stamp.

When Xu Guangtao saw it was Li Luo, he didn't even ask any questions, immediately handing over the stamp. He then watched as Li Luo took the stamp, pressed it twice on his and Ying Chanxi's stamp booklets, and then handed it back.

"Thanks for your hard work." Li Luo patted Xu Guangtao's shoulder and gave Ying Chanxi a grin.

"You're so bad," Ying Chanxi whispered like a thief. "Who cheats like that?"

"If we get to the prize draw early, we might get more chances," Li Luo said. "At worst, we can come back and play again after we're done."

"Fine." Ying Chanxi was quite happy looking at the completely filled stamp booklet in her hand, and she immediately headed for the classroom door.

But just then, upon seeing Li Luo, Yan Zhusheng walked over with the guitar and said to him, "I'm a little tired."

"If you're tired, then take a break," Li Luo said. "Or you can find Xu Yinghuan to walk around the other classes with you."

Yan Zhusheng shook her head and looked at the stamp booklet in Li Luo's hand curiously. "Have you finished playing all of them?"

"Just collected them all." Li Luo waved the booklet in his hand. "But it's already past ten. It's probably too late for you to collect them all."

"Oh." Yan Zhusheng nodded. "But you finished collecting them."

"...What do you mean?"

"I worked very hard this morning," Yan Zhusheng said with a straight face. "Can you let me have one go at the prize draw?"

Li Luo looked at her, somewhat amused. "I was wondering what you were going to say. If you want to try the prize draw, just come with us."

"Okay." Yan Zhusheng nodded and immediately fell into step behind Li Luo.

And so, Ying Chanxi, who was waiting for Li Luo outside the classroom, saw that he had an extra person by his side.

"Why is Zhusheng here too?"

(End of Chapter)
